subject: Another question about fitting linear mixed models

messages.author: b6fd2925353976cd
messages.subject: Another question about fitting linear mixed models
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying to understand the difference between these two lmer models in the context of Stan:

m2<-lmer(rrt~so+(1+so|subj)+(1|item),headnoun)
m3<-lmer(rrt~so+(1|subj)+(so-1|subj)+(1|item),headnoun)

Thanks to Sergio, Bob, and Andrew, I understand now how the prior for the correlation matrix is defined for m2 such that we can get a posterior distribution for the variance covariance matrix of the random effects.

In model m3, we have one variance component for varying intercepts by subject, say:

sigma_u[1] ~ normal(0,5)

and another variance component for slopes, also by subject, say

sigma_u[2] ~ normal(0,5)

Importantly, the correlation parameter is not estimated in m3, i.e., lmer does not print out any correlation value.

For pedagogical reasons, I was wondering whether I can dispense with the variance-covariance matrix completely (and therefore any prior for the correlation matrix). I could simply define two priors for the two components shown above.

When I do this in Stan, I get pretty comparable results with respect to lmer (fully worked example below---my apologies to Bob for not indenting my comments properly). My question is: is this a correct way to fit the model m3, i.e., without specifying a prior for the correlation matrix? Or is it technically incorrect to do this, i.e., is it always necessary to specify such multiple variance components in terms of the variance-covariance matrix? 

Here are the estimates from Stan vs lmer for the variance components in m2 vs m3. The items std deviation is much larger in Stan, but this is not an important detail, the Stan estimate is realistic.

## m2:
##                    Stan  lmer
#subjintercept   0.6  0.610
#subjslope        0.1  0.229
#item                 6.3  0.331 <= don't match 
#error                1.0  0.946
## m3
##                     Stan                              lmer
#subjintercept   0.6                               0.610
#subjslope        0.2 (was 0.1 in m2)     0.229
#item                4.2 (was 6.3 in m2)     0.331 <= don't match
#error               1.0                               0.946

##Code:

## varying intercepts and varying slopes, without correlation (m3):
data<-read.table("gibsonwu2012data.txt",header=T)
## convert to reciprocal rt:
data$rrt<- -1000/data$rt
## contrast coding:
data$so <- ifelse(
  data$type%in%c("subj-ext"),-0.5,0.5)

headnoun.dat <- list(subj=
                       sort(as.integer( 
                         factor(headnoun$subj) )),
                     item=sort(as.integer( 
                       factor(headnoun$item) )),
                     rrt = headnoun$rrt,
                     so = headnoun$so,
                     N = nrow(headnoun),
                     I = 
                       length( unique(headnoun$subj) ),
                     K = 
                       length( unique(headnoun$item) )  
)


varyingintslopes_codev2 <- 'data {
int<lower=1> N;
real rrt[N];   //outcome
real so[N];   //predictor
int<lower=1> I;   //number of subjects
int<lower=1> K;   //number of items
int<lower=1, upper=I> subj[N];  //subject id
int<lower=1, upper=K> item[N];  //item id
}
parameters {
vector[2] beta;      // intercept and slope
vector[2] u[I];   // random intercept and slope
real w[K];   // random intercept item
real<lower=0> sigma_e;  // residual sd 
vector<lower=0>[2] sigma_u;   // subj sd
real<lower=0> sigma_w;   // item sd
}
model {
real mu[N];   // mu for likelihood
for (i in 1:I) u[i,1] ~ normal(0, sigma_u[1]);  
for (i in 1:I) u[i,2] ~ normal(0, sigma_u[2]);  
for (k in 1:K) w[k] ~ normal(0,sigma_w); 
for (n in 1:N) {
mu[n] <- beta[1] + beta[2]*so[n] + u[subj[n], 1] + u[subj[n], 2]*so[n];
}
rrt ~ normal(mu,sigma_e);    // likelihood
beta ~ normal(0,5);
sigma_e ~ normal(0,5);
sigma_u ~ normal(0,5);
sigma_w ~ normal(0,5);
}
'

library(rstan)
set_cppo("fast") 

fitv2 <- stan(model_code = varyingintslopes_codev2, 
            data = headnoun.dat, 
            iter = 1000, chains = 2)

print(fitv2)

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Another question about fitting linear mixed models
parts:
Hi, Shravan. I think that your m3 is a way to have varying intercepts and varying slopes while forcing their correlation to be 0. I'd guess that is a bad idea, it should be better to allow that covariance to be estimated.  But . . . in regular lmer, the cov is estimated by maximum likelihood so it can be unstable.  I think blmer would work better; see here:
http://www.stat.columbia.edu/~gelman/research/unpublished/ms.pdf
In Stan it should be fine because you're averaging over the posterior distribution of the cov matrix rather than using a noisy point estimate.
A
